text: make-it-a-bit-better 是一个 DSH 技能插件，将产品打磨组织成逐轮的小步改进流程。它把随意的“优化一下”转为先接地、头脑风暴、选择一个小改进、实现、验证并记录的循环；每轮聚焦一个角度，并可设置目标仓库、轮数和关注路径。适合希望 agent 持续改进代码产品、同时保留验证和跨轮记录的用户。安装需要兼容版本的 DSH。

make-it-a-bit-better is a DSH skill plugin for iterative product polishing. Each round grounds on a target repository, brainstorms options, implements one small improvement, verifies it, and records the result. Specify a target, round count, and optional focus. Requires a compatible DSH version.
想让 agent 每次只挑一个小改进，逐轮打磨我的产品。
帮我围绕指定功能迭代优化几轮，并在每轮做完检查。
Help me improve a code product through small, brainstormed, verified rounds.
make-it-a-bit-better 的功能「逐轮小步打磨」：每轮先了解目标产品，再头脑风暴并选择一个小角度实现；按用户给定轮数重复，并将较大的想法留待以后处理。通过提示中指定 target、rounds 和可选 focus 来触发。
make-it-a-bit-better 的功能「验证并记录改进」：每轮要求对改动执行真实检查，通过后提交并写入项目级 ledger；失败时先尝试修复，仍失败则撤销该轮改动并记录结果。

A bit better, round after round.

make-it-a-bit-better README · Introduction：A skill plugin that runs an autonomous product-polish loop. Every round opens a **mandatory fresh brainstorm** (3 perspective-forced subagents), picks **one small angle**, implements, verifies and commits it, and logs the round in a per-project ledger. Good ideas that are too big for one round go to an **icebox** instead of being forced in. The philosophy is the name: no rewrites — a bit better, accumulated round after round.
make-it-a-bit-better README · Why not just ask an agent to "improve it"?：An ad-hoc prompt can produce a change; it can't produce this loop's three structural guarantees:
section: Why not just ask an agent to "improve it"?

text:
make-it-a-bit-better README · Why not just ask an agent to "improve it"?：- **A fresh brainstorm every round** — 3 forced perspectives regenerate candidates outside the last round's frame, deduped against the ledger. An ad-hoc prompt re-cooks whatever the model already said.
- **One small, verified change** — ≤3 files / ≈100 lines, a real check must pass, and a red check is reverted rather than shipped. An ad-hoc prompt optimizes for looking done.
- **Memory across rounds** — the ledger records dimensions touched and parks oversized ideas in the icebox, so round 17 doesn't repeat round 3. An ad-hoc prompt restarts from zero every time.
section: Why not just ask an agent to "improve it"?

make-it-a-bit-better README · Inputs：| input | default | what it does |
|-------|---------|--------------|
| `target` | current working directory | repo path to polish. Must be the root of a git repository: a non-git target, or one nested inside another repo, is rejected before any work starts. |
| `rounds N` | 1 | how many rounds to run ("N rounds" or "keep going"). With N given, all N run without asking; after two consecutive thin brainstorms the loop stops itself early. |
| `focus` | none | a feature/path to spotlight (e.g. a just-shipped feature). Shapes generation in every lens and ranks in-focus candidates first — not just where the round grounds. |

make-it-a-bit-better README · What a round looks like：1. **Ground** — read the product, recent commits and the ledger; dimensions never touched get priority. A non-git target is rejected up front, before any work is done. A repo with no README/docs grounds on entry-point code + tree instead — and says so in the round report, never improvising a product summary.
2. **Brainstorm (mandatory)** — 3 fresh subagents, each wearing a different lens (first-time user, picky daily user, maintainer-in-six-months, auditor, automation caller, …), each returning candidate angles; deduped against the ledger so nothing gets re-cooked. Without a subagent tool it falls back to three in-session, lens-forced passes. A run with `focus` spotlights that area in every lens's grounding. Still thin after widening the lenses? A good icebox idea that slices into the round cap gets promoted instead of letting the run stop early.
3. **Select one** — felt-impact × freshness ÷ cost, capped at ≤3 files / ≈100 lines per round. Bigger ideas → icebox. With `focus`, in-focus candidates rank first.
4. **Implement** — target-repo conventions, complete changes only, no TODO/mock leftovers.

make-it-a-bit-better README · The ledger：`.agents/mabb/ledger.md` in the target repo is the loop's memory. It prevents repeating old angles and carries a coverage view that keeps steering the brainstorm toward untouched dimensions. The icebox holds good-but-too-big ideas until you promote them to real projects — a round that lands one deletes its entry, so the icebox always lists what is still pending. Icebox entries carry short ids (`IB-1`, `IB-2`, …, stable once assigned), so reports, next-round hints and promotions cite an entry exactly instead of describing it.

make-it-a-bit-better README · Side effects (disclosed for review)：- **Model calls**: each round spawns 3 short-lived brainstorm subagents (falls back to three in-session passes when the client has no subagent tool) — N rounds means ≈3N such calls.
- **Files**: writes the improvement itself in the target repo, plus the local ledger under `<target>/.agents/mabb/`.
- **Git**: one local commit per round in the target repo (exactly two when a round fails: the round's commit, then its revert — the failed diff stays in history, nothing ships unverified). Shared/team repos get a branch proposal first — never a direct main commit. **Never pushes** to any remote unless you explicitly say push.
- **Network**: none beyond the model API.
- **Context**: the skill text is loaded whole by the executor every round, so it carries a soft cap (150 lines) — growth past the cap pays for itself by distilling existing lines, keeping rounds loadable for small-context agents.

make-it-a-bit-better README · Install：**DSH** — this repo is a DSH bundle: one package mounts the `make-it-a-bit-better` skill (pure skill — no MCP server, no runtime dependencies). Requires DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` or newer.

```bash
make-it-a-bit-better README · From a checkout：dsh plugin add /path/to/make-it-a-bit-better

make-it-a-bit-better README · Once published：dsh plugin add make-it-a-bit-better
```

**ZCode** — the same repo doubles as a ZCode plugin (`.zcode-plugin/plugin.json` + `skills/`): install it from any marketplace that lists it — for a local tryout, a dev marketplace pointing at a checkout works.

make-it-a-bit-better README · Quick start：With the plugin installed:

> Run 3 rounds of make it a bit better on /path/to/repo

Or with the steering wheel: point it at a repo, ask for N rounds, spotlight one area:

> Run 5 rounds of make it a bit better on /path/to/repo, focusing on the checkout flow

make-it-a-bit-better README · Quick start：Expect: a ledger row per round and up to 3 committed small improvements — *up to*, because the loop self-stops after two consecutive thin brainstorms (the ledger gets a dated `stalled` line) and a red check it can't fix is reverted (a `failed, reverted` row, nothing shipped). Fewer commits than N is the loop being honest, not broken. An icebox appears only when the brainstorm produced ideas too big for one round.
